Meanwhile, RTX ( NYSE:RTX ) stock is up 0.52% to $193.15. The gap stands out because both companies sell engines into the same commercial aviation market, pointing to a selloff rooted in GE Aerospace's own quarter.
On the surface, GE Aerospace delivered a clean quarter. Its Q3 2026 adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.25 beat the $1.99 consensus estimate, and revenue of $14.12 billion topped the $12.84 billion analysts expected.
Management raised GE Aerospace's full-year 2026 guidance across the board. That outlook now calls for adjusted EPS of $8 to $8.10, up from a prior range of $7.65 to $7.85. Targets for operating profit and free cash flow moved higher as well.
Beneath those headline figures, GE Aerospace's costs are climbing fast. GE Aerospace's sales discounts and allowances rose sharply on new engine installations, spare parts and durability reserves. The company's cash generation slid too, with free cash flow falling 9.2% year over year to $2.04 billion while operating income barely moved at $2.81 billion.
Many successful investors eventually reach the same moment. The saving is done, the portfolio is built, and the question quietly changes from how much can I grow this to how much can I take out? Get that second question wrong and decades of good investing can come apart in a handful of years.
That is exactly what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps answer. It covers what your retirement could actually cost, which income sources are worth using, and the withdrawal math that decides whether the money lasts. It is free today from Fisher Investments. Read More Here ›
Mix and inflation also weighed on GE Aerospace margins, partially offsetting gains from higher volume and pricing. Separately, the company deferred revenue recognition on its GE9X engine pending midseal certification, which adds one more open question to an already complex cost story.
Chief executive H. Lawrence Culp Jr. struck an upbeat tone as GE Aerospace posted its results. "Thanks to the collaboration of the GE Aerospace team with our supplier partners we continue to build momentum," Culp stated. He also pointed to record internal shop visit output and an agreement to acquire Consolidated Precision Products, a castings supplier, to expand capacity.
GE Aerospace now expects commercial services revenue to grow at a low-double-digit rate in 2027. That forecast rests on what Culp called the company's "over $170 billion commercial services backlog," which gives the services business deep visibility into future work.
Demand is holding firm at GE Aerospace, with total orders up 49% to $19 billion in the quarter. Its commercial services orders climbed 23%, and the company keeps spending over $3 billion a year on research and development.
GE Aerospace makes most of its profit servicing commercial jet engines over their working lives, while RTX pairs its engines with defense systems. Boeing ( NYSE:BA ) builds the aircraft those engines power. A service-heavy model like GE Aerospace's puts parts allowances and durability reserves close to the center of its earnings, which helps explain why the cost jump hurts. Boeing shares are down 0.49% to $190.57.
Across the sector, the iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense ETF ( CBOE:ITA ) is down 0.4% to $206.90. That far smaller decline marks the GE Aerospace stock selloff as company-specific.
Furthermore, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ( NYSEARCA:SPY ) is down by only 0.1% to $765.92. With the broad market nearly flat, macro weakness explains little of the slide in GE Aerospace shares.
GE Aerospace still faces the question of whether allowances and durability reserves ease next quarter. Midseal certification for the GE9X is the other open variable, since GE Aerospace can't recognize that engine's deferred revenue until it comes.
As long as those costs keep climbing, GE Aerospace stock could stay volatile around each quarterly report. Position sizes should stay small until GE Aerospace's cost picture resolves.

articles.content_orig:

Your newsletter sign-up was successful
Samsung's latest wave of foldables was incredibly popular. Okay, the Fold 8 took everything by storm, but that might not stop the company from doubling up on its offerings next year.
A rumor on X from tipster TheGalox claims Samsung is preparing for its "biggest foldable lineup ever" in 2027 (via 9to5Google ). To start things off, TheGalox claims the Galaxy Z TriFold 2 could start Samsung's huge foldable stampede in 2027. This would succeed the original Z TriFold, which Samsung stopped producing after three months. Elsewhere, the tipster claims the foldables we typically expect could expand.
Currently, Samsung offers three foldables: the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Fold 8 Ultra, and Flip 8. The Fold 8 is its short, wider addition, and the Fold 8 Ultra is its standard book-style foldable. However, the tipster suggests Samsung could slip in a "Galaxy Z Fold 9 Pro." It's unclear what this would be. What's more, we're unsure about how Samsung would position this device between the Fold 9 and Fold 9 Ultra.
While we also expect to see a Flip 9, rumors say Samsung could introduce a new type of foldable: the "Galaxy Z Slide." It's almost a shame that the most interesting-sounding device is shrouded in the largest shadow, but that's only half true. If we want to at least fathom where we might go, we'll have to look back to CES 2025.
The Fold 8 was popular was an understandable reason. It's slightly smaller (shorter), and it felt nice to use for consumers. However, I'm curious about public reception for the Slide, if it's even happening. As a concept, the device seems really interesting. But concepts don't always transfer well into reality. These phones have to be practical, not just cool. Also, what would its price be? We all know how prices are skyrocketing.
Samsung Display was at CES 2025, if you remember our coverage about it (if you don't, here it is ). As usual, the company, like other companies, showed off several prototypes. On display were the "Slidable Flex Duet" and "Solo." The Slidable Flex Duet (YouTube) would let users pull (or slide) its display out from the left and right. The device would sit at 8 inches when compact, but sliding out its display would bring it to 12.4 inches—very tablet-like.
Alternatively, you have the Solo, which would go from 13 inches to 17.3 inches. Whether or not Samsung develops one of these concepts remains to be seen. This only serves as a base to get our minds thinking.
Rumors about a TriFold sequel got underway quickly after Apple 's iPhone Duo launch. Allegedly, this phone could debut in 2027 with a thinner, lighter, and more durable design. However, its price tag might remain pretty hefty at $2,800.

articles.title_orig: Salesforce deepens AI bets with $5.66 billion Braze deal
articles.title_zh: Salesforce deepens AI bets with $5.66 billion Braze deal
articles.content_orig:
Shares of Salesforce slipped roughly 1% on Tuesday morning, after the company announced an agreement to buy customer engagement platform Braze for about $5.66 billion.
Under the deal, holders of Braze Class A common stock will get $47.50 in cash per share. The transaction is expected to close in fiscal 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, according to a Salesforce blog .
Braze shares closed at $30.04 on Monday. The stock skyrocketed more than 50% on Tuesday after a brief halt premarket following the news. The company makes artificial intelligence marketing tools to manage customer data and messaging.
"Salesforce shares our commitment to marketers, and we'll continue building as Braze and investing in the Braze community of customers and partners who built this company with us," Bill Magnuson, CEO of Braze, said in a statement. "Salesforce's platform will help us innovate faster and together we'll help marketers around the world build deeper, more lasting relationships with their customers."
The latest deal comes just months after Salesforce announced it would buy AI customer service platform Fin for about $3.6 billion, in a move meant to bolster the company's agentic AI offerings for enterprises.
In August, Salesforce and Anthropic announced an expanded partnership , including a new plugin called "Claudeforce" with pre-built sales skills for salespeople to better compose emails, update records and more with the frontier lab's model.

articles.title_orig: Here's What Apple's Apps Look Like on the iPhone Duo
articles.title_zh: Here's What Apple's Apps Look Like on the iPhone Duo
articles.content_orig:
With just three days to go until the iPhone Duo is released, Apple is getting ready for the launch. Behind the scenes, the App Store now has screenshots of Apple's built-in apps running on the Duo. We've seen some apps in marketing materials, but images of the ones we haven't seen give us an idea of what it will be like using the ‌iPhone Duo‌ day to day.
Many apps are shown in landscape orientation with an iPad-like interface that uses some of the screen real estate for sidebar navigation. Other apps use the full screen for more viewing space.
Some apps have a dual view that goes beyond sidebar navigation. In Contacts, the app is divided into a list of names and a view for editing information.
The Siri app doesn't have a traditional sidebar, but it also doesn't get a full split. The left part of the interface is a tiled view of conversations, while the full conversation can be viewed on the right.
The ‌iPhone Duo‌ adopts a vertical dock and vertical navigation bars on the right side of the display in both open and closed views. The exception is an open view with the ‌iPhone Duo‌ held vertically, similar to an iPad in portrait orientation. When positioned that way, navigation bars remain at the bottom of the interface.
Apple's screenshots don't show many apps in the unfolded vertical orientation, but it is a viewing option. Apple says it's ideal for apps that use the keyboard or for browsing in Safari.
Apps like Preview have palettes at the bottom for selecting tools, and those are combined with sidebars, navigation bars, or both. Markup editing gives a good preview of what drawing and photo editing apps will be like, with a large amount of display space paired with a bottom tool palette.
Apps that don't need large navigation bars have widescreen views that take up the whole display. Apps that do have navigation bars have an option to tap to hide the bar.
Floating popovers show up when you press and hold on an icon. The popovers aren't scaled up and take up less room on the display than they do on Apple's smaller iPhones.
When you're on the Home Screen , you'll see the Today view on the left of the display with your widgets, while app icons are on the right. The status bar is in the upper-right corner, and the Lock Screen icons like Flashlight and Camera are in the bottom right. The inner display doesn't have an always-visible Dynamic Island because there is no Face ID and the FaceTime camera is under the screen. Apple is still using the ‌Dynamic Island‌, which expands out from the side of the display for Live Activities and alerts. The outer display has a small vertical ‌Dynamic Island‌ that includes the camera cutout.
Most of the ‌App Store‌ screenshots have the ‌iPhone Duo‌ unfolded in landscape orientation, though some also show what apps will look like on the smaller outer display.
Apps will be able to transition quickly from open to closed and to different positions, and Apple made an effort to keep navigation buttons in the same place for a unified experience no matter how you're using it.
Open and closed aren't the only options for the ‌iPhone Duo‌. Few screenshots show the positions, but the Duo can be used laptop-style at an angle for watching videos or standing in a tent shape with the outer display visible. You can also use it partially open and held like a book.
Screenshots also don't show two apps used side by side or multiple windows of the same app like Safari, both of which are options. We'll see a deluge of ‌iPhone Duo‌ updates for third-party apps when the device comes out.
The ‌iPhone Duo‌ is launching on October 23, which is this Friday. We should be getting media reviews and first impressions as soon as tomorrow since we'll be two days out from release.

articles.title_orig: ID@XBOX x IGN Showcase Recap: All the News and Announcements
articles.title_zh: ID@XBOX x IGN Showcase Recap: All the News and Announcements
articles.content_orig:
A brand-new ID@Xbox Showcase Presented by IGN has arrived, and it was filled with exciting upcoming games you won't want to miss. From remasters/director's cuts of Shrek 2, The Wolf Among Us, and Zero Parades to games about shredding paper (Paper Shredder!), tongue-grappling and pinball-bouncing (Croak), and digging holes (A Game About Digging a Hole Together), there it a lot to look forward to.
To ensure you don't miss a thing, we've gathered all the announcements and reveals in one place for you to check out! Let us know which was your favorite!
Shrek 2 Remastered is bringing our favorite ogre back to the spotlight, and it will allow players to relive iconic moments and visit memorable locations from the film. Enjoy new graphics, new features, and more when Shrek 2 Remastered launches on November 10, 2026, on Xbox Series X/S.
The Big Bad Wolf is back in The Wolf Among Us Remastered, and you can check how this new version of the 2013 classic looks in action. The remaster comes with enhances visuals, upgraded animation and audio, an all-new Noir Mode, behind-the-scenes content, playable deleted scenes, a redesigned werewolf form for Bigby, and more.
The Wolf Among Us Remastered will be released on October 29, 2026.
Zero Parades: Director's Cut will be released on November 3, 2026, on Xbox Series X/S and PC, and this new trailer features gameplay from the espionage RPG developed by ZA/UM. It's almost time to face you one final mission and all the trials and tribulations that come with it.
Check out the reveal trailer for Magenta Down, a sci-fi atmospheric adventure game where players must traverse a harsh, remote exoplanet to endure injury and radiation exposure with scarce supplies.
Magenta Down will be released on Xbox Series X/S and PC in 2027.
Tongue-grapple and pinball-bounce to your heart's content in Croak, an upcoming hand-drawn 2D precision platformer game coming to PC and Xbox Series X/S in March 2027. Players become a frog prince and aim to reach the Witch's Banquet, fighting bosses, finding collectibles, and more along the way.
Feast your eyes on the Shine Level of Mr. Records to see more of George's upcoming adventure. Who is George? An old dreamer with an extraordinary gift that lets him transcend through music.
Mr. Records will be released on PC and Xbox Series X/S in Spring 2027.
Bosses and gameplay from Chronoscript: The Endless End take center stage in this new trailer that showcases the upcoming exploration-based action-adventure game comprised of two worlds: a 3D-rendered grand residence littered with thousands of manuscript pages, and the 2D pen-and-ink illustrated worlds within them.
Chronoscript: The Endless End will be released on Xbox Series X/S and PC in early summer 2027. It is also coming to PS5.
Say hello to Love Is A Roguelite (or LIAR for short), an upcoming game that mixes turn-based tactics, deck-building, and dating, all set within a procedurally generated Love Story. Your choices matter thanks to the proprietary LoveSync system, so choose wisely!
Love Is A Roguelite launches in Fall 2027 on Xbox Series X/S and PC.
New gameplay has been revealed for Drill Keeper, the upcoming deck-building roguelike siege defense game that see players traversing the galaxy to secure vital resources for their people. Protect your mining operations, design labyrinthine pathways and traps to halt your foes, and more.
Drill Keep will be released on PC Game Pass in summer 2027.
Mr. Magpie's Harmless Card Game received a new trailer and gave a new glimpse at the sinister roguelike deckbuilding where you'll "build your deck, push your luck, and combine powerful synergies to tip the odds in your favour.
Mr. Magpie's Harmless Card Game Xbox Series X/S and PC in early 2027.
Waveling Island is an upcoming cozy creature-collecting game that features hand-drawn pixel-art and an island filled with mysterious creatures.
Waveling Island is headed to Xbox Series X/S and PC soon.
It's always more fun with friends, especially when digging a hole! In A Game About Digging a Hole Together, you'll be able to dig a hole at a beach with your friends. Dig together, collect resources, sell them, upgrade your equipment, and search for the promised buried treasure.
A Game About Digging a Hole Together will be available on Xbox Series X/S and Xbox on PC on December 4, 2026, and PC via Steam, PS5, Nintendo Switch 2 at a later date.
Scramble Knights Online is coming to Xbox Series X/S and PC on October 26, 2026, and to celebrate the release date, a new trailer was released that showed off new gameplay for the MMO-lite action RPG. Get ready to step into the kingdom of Terracott as a knight-in-training and embark on a grand adventure.
Paper Shredded is an incremental game where players need to shred their company's paperwork to earn a $1,000,000 payout. Shred, sweep, upgrade, and cut down tower-high piles of confidential records to uncover what's hidden below.
Paper Shredder will be released on Xbox Series X/S and PC in winter 2026.
Embark on an adventure in Vanran, an upcoming dark fantasy action RPG where a human slave in the Demon Realm wields a sealed blade and rises in rebellion.
Vanran will be released on Xbox Series X/S and PC in 2027.
Rustown, the upcoming story-driven action-adventure game, has been given a release date of June 30, 2027, on PC and Xbox Series X/S. Check out this new trailer to see the game in action, which happens to be set in a slum inhabited by infected outcasts suffering from cognitive decline. Avoid danger without fighting, uncover clues, and try to find your missing father.
Vampire spy house leader Daddy introduces us to the recently resurrected Fritz and the team you'll lead in this latest trailer for Red Kiss. From developer Wispfire, Red Kiss is a tactical narrative RPG where you'll have to dispatch a team of vampire spies through the tense and fractured streets of Cold War Berlin.
Red Fritz will be released on Xbox Series X/S and PC in 2027.
Get ready to solve the case in Graytail, an upcoming mystery action-adventure title set within a 2.5D pixel-art world. After a famous pilot vanishes over the Pacific, a detective with a headache that never stops embarks on a journey to find them with the pilot's daughter in tow.
Graytail will be released on Xbox Series X/S and PC in November 2027.
Check out this sizzle reel to learn about three exciting upcoming games - Arctic Eggs, Mouthwashing, and No, I'm Not Human.
Arctic (October 20, 2026) has you frying eggs on Mount Everest, Mouthwashing (October 29, 2026) has you taking responsibility for a dying crew of a shipwrecked space freighter, and No, I'm Not Human (2027) has your interrogating door-knocking strangers to spot deadly shape-shifting imposters.
Adam Bankhurst is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on X/Twitter @AdamBankhurst, Instagram, and TikTok, and listen to his show, Talking Disney Magic.

articles.title_orig: Sundar Pichai: Google’s Frontier Imperative, Compute Scarcity Dilemmas, Future AI Products and Businesses
articles.title_zh: Sundar Pichai: Google’s Frontier Imperative, Compute Scarcity Dilemmas, Future AI Products and Businesses
articles.content_orig:
Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai has little patience for doubts about Google’s willingness or capacity to compete at the frontier of AI.
His company’s latest Gemini 4 Argon model — long-promised and recently delivered — beats OpenAI and Anthropic’s latest public models on coding, math, science, and knowledge-work benchmarks and has placed Google’s AI back among the world’s best.
Amid chatter that Google was fine with good-enough lightweight ‘Flash’ models, Pichai pushed back hard against any suggestion that company is limiting its research ambitions. “We won’t do it any other way,” he told me in a Big Technology Podcast interview recorded this week at Google’s Mountain View headquarters.
Pursuing cutting-edge research is costly for Google, requiring compute and chips that otherwise could be sold at a high markup by its cloud business. But Pichai said allocating resources to frontier AI development is “ground zero” for Google.
“Our cloud business is at any given moment in time forgoing short-term revenues because we are making compute trade-offs to support frontier AI development,” Pichai told me.
In our conversation, we discussed Argon (which Pichai says processed three times as many tokens as Gemini 3 in the 72 hours after launch), AI’s role in developing better models, the AI interface of the future, competition with OpenAI, Google’s partnerships with Anthropic and Apple, data centers in space, and the nature of his optimism.
You can read the full conversation, lightly edited for length and clarity, below, or listen to it on Apple Podcasts , Spotify , YouTube , or your podcast app of choice .
Alex Kantrowitz: Google is back at the frontier with Gemini 4 Argon, which beats OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s public models on benchmarks spanning coding, math, science, and knowledge work.
The conventional wisdom was that Google had given up on the frontier to focus on fast, good-enough models for its products. That was wrong?
Sundar Pichai: Very wrong. Look, we are so committed to being at the frontier. It’s in our DNA. We won’t do it any other way. We’ve been thinking about the AI frontier for well over a decade now.
The frontier is very dynamic. It’s very competitive. It’s very exciting. I couldn’t be more pleased with how Argon has come together. We took our time with it. We made sure we tested it safely and deployed it carefully. We took a bit longer than our other models, given its capabilities.
Across the board, be it for agentic work, knowledge work, coding, creative tasks, Argon is one of the really good frontier models. The first 72 hours since we launched, it’s almost up to 25 trillion tokens used, which is about three times what Gemini 3.0 had in the first 72 hours. And we are capacity constrained as we are serving it.
Excited, but there are always areas….. You know, the frontier is very dynamic, and you have to keep evolving the models. There are areas which we can see we need to improve as well. We’ll be at work on all of that as well.
On any given model, Argon would be across the board better at everything if you just look even two months back. But the space is so evolving. Even on coding, for example, there are pockets where we know we need to do better, and there’s clear feedback. We’ll make it better.
The argument for standard models is that they’re already good enough to build great products, with the frontier valuable only for certain tasks. Meta built Muse with good models rather than the best, and Google could put standard models into Maps, Gmail, and Search. Why isn’t that sufficient?
It’s definitely not how I have thought about it at all. We are deeply committed to driving the state of the art and actually pushing where this technology can go, all the way from transformers. That’s a journey we’ve been on. You will see us continue to do that.
When you’re at the frontier, you get an earlier look into the emerging capabilities, earlier than others, which helps you better prepare for the future. We are fortunate to have a wide set of opportunities across consumer and enterprise. Some of our cloud customers, for sure, want the model at the frontier.
The frontier models will be better at developing the next set of models in an era of recursive self-improvement. I would argue it matters there. Internally, we have definitely seen a steep point of inflection by deploying Argon to our developers. It definitely tackles problems which our previous models could not do. Being at the frontier puts you at the innovation frontier and helps you drive that as well.
There is room for models of all sizes and capabilities. That’s why we did Flash, Flash-Lite, etc. I agree with you that you can develop very good product experiences with not necessarily the most frontier model, because they tend to be slower and more expensive too. But we care about the Pareto frontier, and we’re committed to doing all of that.
You said developing frontier models gives you a look at what’s coming. What do you see on the horizon?
What makes this moment so exciting is you build something which you think is a culmination of months of work, and you put it out. You already see clear headroom ahead.
We’ve all been working on these agentic, long-horizon capabilities, but clearly the frontier is going to have multiple of these agents working together to do things. That’s an example of an exciting paradigm underway.
It’s also clear to me that users, both in consumer and enterprise, will have access to some multi-agent framework for them, working all the time doing things. It feels like a moment of infinite possibilities.
Sergey Brin said one of Argon’s core innovations was relying more on the model to help develop the model. Yet incidents involving OpenAI’s bots breaking containment and Google’s bots accessing a site they shouldn’t have suggest these systems still aren’t perfectly aligned. Isn’t there reasonable cause for concern about accelerating toward recursive self-improvement?
There are three parts to your question. Let’s first talk about RSI itself. You’re right, Sergey mentioned RSI being a critical contributor as we are developing Argon. But to be very clear, today, in a continuum, we are pretty far from the end state of RSI or something like that.
The right way to describe it is you have RSI loops along with AI researchers in various aspects of model development. You almost have agents helping AI researchers in some automated way work together to build these models. It’s good to at least understand where we are today, and it’s super exciting. I expect that continuum to keep making progress as we go into next year.
The second question is around safety. Security comes from defense in depth. You’re talking about alignment, obviously. We all are doing a lot of work to make sure the models are as aligned as possible. But it’s an active area of research, and there are clear gaps.
That’s not the only thing we rely on. You have the work you do on alignment, but beyond that, we put a lot of effort into real-time monitoring as these models are working. Making sure you have good telemetry into what’s happening so that you can intervene in real time if you see unexpected behaviors.
How you do that, the architecture with which you do that, how you make sure it’s all sandboxed and isolated in a way that it can continue doing its job during real-time monitoring — these are all areas of investment.
Obviously, when we deploy these models, giving customers, enterprises, control, both with real-time monitoring, but their ability to decide where they deploy, what type of data which models ever have access to, etc. All that work is very, very important, and we are doing a lot of that.
As an industry, we need to constantly up our game and take the time to do all this stuff, including dedicating the compute required to make sure you can safely deploy these models.
The third part is: Is it all enough? This is why there are a lot of conversations in the industry, and I think it’s reasonable to be worried. T

articles.title_orig: 2 men rearrested in UK on suspicion of assisting Iran over suspected plot at a US-run air base
articles.title_zh: 2 men rearrested in UK on suspicion of assisting Iran over suspected plot at a US-run air base
articles.content_orig:
British counterterrorism police said Tuesday they have rearrested two men in their investigation into last month’s incident at RAF Fairford in England, where US B-1 bombers were based.
A 24-year-old British national and a 25-year-old dual British-Iranian national were rearrested on suspicion of assisting Iran’s foreign intelligence service, police said in a statement.
“So far seven men have been arrested in connection with our investigation,” Laurence Taylor, a senior counterterrorism police officer, said in a statement. “As a result of the ongoing efforts of our officers, earlier today two of those men were re-arrested for offences relating to Section 3 of the National Security Act — assisting a foreign intelligence service.”
“This is very much a live investigation, and our evidence gathering continues, but at this time our position remains the same; we consider it highly likely that there is Iranian state involvement,” Taylor added. The other five men are currently out on bail. Police have not released the names of any of them.
In late September, British authorities announced the initial arrest of five men “on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act” and explosives offenses near RAF Fairford, a British air base long used by the US Air Force. Army bomb disposal units and police officers swarmed the area and evacuated civilian homes around the base.
Earlier this month, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that the suspected plot targeting RAF Fairford was “almost certainly directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard.” Iran has firmly rejected the accusations.
US President Donald Trump praised the arrests at the time, telling reporters that the US had worked with Britain and that the men arrested were planning to do “big damage” to RAF Fairford.
“We had them under view for a long time, and we got them,” Trump said. US intelligence had tracked planning by Iranian groups to target US assets at the base weeks ahead of any arrests, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter.
Residents around RAF Fairford also may have tipped authorities off. One resident, who asked to remain anonymous, told CNN that she had called police after seeing three vans surrounded by eight to 10 masked men blocking her driveway.
In an interview with Sky News, British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting thanked the woman for making the emergency call. He mentioned that she had only a “partial picture” and offered no further details.
Developments at the base did not end there. Days after the initial arrests, the US moved all of its long-range bombers from RAF Fairford following an unspecified threat, a knowledgeable source said.
At the time, Trump and Vice President JD Vance hinted that a threat against US assets had prompted the move.
“I think we can say that — I mean, they didn’t fly out by accident,” Trump said. “There were some threats, and rather than tempting the enemy, we’ll capture the enemy and beat the enemy. But why should we leave them there? So we moved them around a little bit.”
Vance said the move was made “out of an abundance of caution,” suggesting it was a response to a potential threat from Iran even as he declined to detail the specific concerns.
As of Tuesday, none of the US bombers had returned to Fairford.
This is a developing story and will be updated.
CNN’s Piper Hudspeth Blackburn, Zachary Cohen and Jennifer Hansler contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: China’s Long Shadow over Washington’s Russian Diesel Deal
articles.title_zh: China’s Long Shadow over Washington’s Russian Diesel Deal
articles.content_orig:
On October 9, the US Treasury issued General License 135 (GL135), authorizing transactions involving Russian-origin diesel until April 7, 2027. On October 13, just four days after GL135 was issued, a tanker transporting roughly 40,000 tonnes of ultra-low-sulfur diesel was en route from the Baltic port of Primorsk toward Morocco. The destination of this shipment was not coincidental either, with the African country having struggled to procure diesel and petrol since the start of the Iran war.
In this sense, GL135 changes the economic calculus for countries that have had to keep their energy ties with Moscow politically or commercially opaque in order to preserve their traditionally close relation with the US and avoid straining relations with the EU. Moreover, the Moroccan case suggests that international sanctions regimes may have limited leverage over third countries once the threat of US enforcement is removed . So, although many US allies were already importing fuel from Russia (Figure 1), GL135 will affect the steep discount and simplify the logistic arrangements that characterized those transactions.
Therefore, the likeliest near-term consequence of GL135 is rerouting barrels that might otherwise have gone elsewhere to US-aligned countries and, possibly, reducing the discount at which Russian diesel traded because of sanctions-related risks, although global supply barely budges . In other words, two seemingly contradictory outcomes can coexist: the pressure on regions struggling to source fuel may ease as diesel shipments from Russia become easier to arrange and reach more buyers, yet the global market balance changes little. Still, the less discussed question is whether easier access to Russian diesel may have been deemed necessary to weaken Chinaâs leverage over fuel-short buyers.
The origins of GL135 should be understood through the interaction between US domestic political pressure and global market imbalances. Indeed, US domestic politics may itself be partly a consequence of the global diesel supply shock, given that disruptions to shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have contributed to US retail diesel prices reaching levels not seen since 2008. Nevertheless, the timing makes the domestic political dimension difficult to ignore: the move came weeks before the midterm elections, when high diesel prices had become a political liability for Republicans.
The geoeconomic rationale behind GL135 is potentially even more relevant, albeit less discussed. Over the summer, China helped cap oil prices by limiting its imports of crude and, given a supply shock is now hitting another market tightly linked to that for oil, one could have expected Beijing to help stabilize the global economy again. Not least because Chinese commercial inventories of middle distillates, a category including diesel and jet fuel, are down just 8.4% from October 2025 . However, Chinaâs willingness to mitigate the crude-supply shock correlated with a different set of market circumstances, not least the USâs ability to increase production to avoid domestic shocks and alleviate scarcity through its strategic reserves. Instead, this time China is prioritizing its energy security by shoring up its strategic reserves and by restricting and tightly managing diesel exports. As a result, Beijing commands enough refining capacity to â bail out the diesel marketâ and it has acquired new leverage over fuel-importing countries that are increasingly exposed to its supply decisions.
Start with this week’s Geopolitics Weekly for free.
Meanwhile, the US has not increased its supply enough to help the Philippines , Morocco , Tunisia , and other allies struggling to secure enough fuel to keep their economy running (Figure 2). Not least because rising prices at home reflect the level of US commercial inventories of refined petroleum products, which are over 10 million barrels lower than last year and regional stocks are up to 32% below the 2021-25 seasonal average. Crucially, the US has got less leverage in the diesel market than for crude, where releases from the strategic reserves and increased output can readily materialize. Moreover, a rapid increase in domestic refining is unlikely given that US refineries are already operating close to the mid-90% in utilization and there is no idle capacity that can come online on short notice. Rather, declining stocks are chiefly due to the closure or conversion to biofuel of several refineries across the country partly motivated by âgreenâ policies. According to one estimate, seven major closures and conversions have removed roughly 1.235 million barrels per day of US refining capacity, more than 6.5% of the total, making external supply disruptions more consequential.
Seen in this context, GL135 appears not just as an electoral maneuver, but also as an effort to reduce Chinese leverage on global diesel supplies by allowing buyers facing prohibitive prices to tap more openly into Russiaâs exports. However, the move will not materially balance the global diesel balance because the binding constraint remains operational refining capacity. Moreover, Moscow does not appear able to release large quantities of diesel into the market, let alone enough to match the scale of Chinaâs reduced exports, given that Ukraine continues to carry out attacks on Russian refineries. Still, the case of Morocco offers an early indication that removing sanctions on Russian diesel may grant some US allies temporary relief from domestic and regional diesel shortages even if the global market imbalance is not corrected any time soon and Russian refining capacity does not recover .
Having settled the origins of GL135, the next question is who benefits from the rerouting of hundreds of thousands of tonnes of diesel to buyers in undersupplied fuel markets.
GL135 widens the set of eligible partners from which fuel can be imported by removing the sanction-risk associated with Russian-origin diesel. However, several analysts tend to agree that a mere reallocation of existing barrels cannot solve supply bottlenecks in the diesel market as effectively as a recovery in refinery output in the US and Russia, unblocking traffic through Hormuz, or a liberalization of Chinese diesel exports. So, the answer depends less on the number of Russian barrels being traded than on how the value of those sales is redistributed.
Given that global supply remains insufficient to balance an inelastic demand and even oil producers like Russia and the US have struggled to add refining capacity, as Russian diesel gets rerouted the main near-term effect may instead be a redistribution of profits. The main reason Russian producersâ revenues could grow in the short term is that the sanction risk likely translated into a discount on the sale price of diesel, as it has done for crude oil. These price cuts drove exportersâ netbacks down. To further complicate matters, Russian exporters do not typically pay for insurance and freight, since their oil and fuels are sold on âfree-on-boardâ (FOB) terms, yet the sellerâs netback can still be affected indirectly by changes in freight and insurance. Practically, buyersâ willingness and ability to pay can limit the sellersâ ability to pass freight and insurance costs through and reduce its netback. Hence, the extensive sanctions with which the G7 established for maritime service providers working with Russian oil companies, put further downward pressure on the latterâs netbacks.
In fact, while the product was being sold at a discount, freight cost rose to cover the so-called âshadow-fleet premiumâ that shippers demanded as compensation for the sanctions and compliance risks. So, as long as those sanctions were backed by the threat of US enforcement, including through tariffs , part of the margin that would otherwise have accrued to Russian sellers shifted to logistics operators and intermediaries.

articles.title_orig: China threatens retaliation if U.K. follows the EU on tariffs
articles.title_zh: China threatens retaliation if U.K. follows the EU on tariffs
articles.content_orig:
LONDON — Beijing has threatened to retaliate if the U.K. raises tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles, aligning with the European Union.
Responding to POLITICO’s story that Britain was looking to act in “lockstep” with the bloc to counter China’s market dominance in electric cars, a spokesperson from the Chinese Ministry of Commerce said : “If the U.K. insists on imposing restrictions on Chinese electric vehicles, China will resolutely retaliate and safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese industries.”
The U.K. is currently working with its European partners to avoid a 10% electric vehicle tariff from the beginning of next year, when stricter rules of origin under the Brexit trade deal kick in.
The British government is also lobbying to be included in the EU’s Made in Europe policies, which give Brussels-made products preferential treatment in certain procurement projects.
U.K. Trade Minister Anas Sarwar told POLITICO on the sidelines of the German-British Business Summit at Mansion House last week that “the more that the U.K. and the EU work together and act in lockstep, the better it is for both the U.K. and the European Union.”
“The automotive sector and partnership remain strong, but do we have to grapple with the challenge that comes from rapid expansion in China? Of course we do,” he added.
China urged Britain to follow World Trade Organization rules and warned it against copying Brussels’ approach, arguing that tariffs on Chinese EVs would be discriminatory.
“China urges the U.K. to abide by WTO rules, think carefully, and not follow the European Union,” said the Chinese Ministry of Commerce spokesperson. “China will closely monitor the U.K.’s developments.”

articles.title_orig: China-Laos air base could be another Southeast Asian forward outpost for Beijing
articles.title_zh: China-Laos air base could be another Southeast Asian forward outpost for Beijing
articles.content_orig:
A new joint military training facility in Laos could give Beijing a lasting foothold in mainland Southeast Asia even without an immediate boost to its combat power, analysts told Radio Free Asia.
Beijing and Vientiane opened a joint support and training center and an aviation academy at Ban Keun, about 50 kilometers north of the Lao capital, on Sept. 29. Beijing says the facility will train Lao air force pilots and it will be maintained by both countries.
The airfield, once complete, would be China’s second joint military outpost in Southeast Asia, after a Chinese-funded expansion of Cambodia’s Ream Naval Base opened in April of last year. The facility at Ream, despite its official designation as a dual-use facility, has seen a regular rotation of Chinese naval vessels.
The joint facility in Laos could allow China to deepen military ties, familiarize personnel with overseas operations and lay the groundwork for a larger presence, Joseph Kristanto, a research analyst at Singapore’s S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, told RFA.
“Ultimately, I think the more important question is not simply whether Ban Keun could accommodate Chinese military aircraft, but whether Beijing intends to develop the facility into a sustained operational hub,” he said.
China’s Defense Ministry said in an announcement that the facility would be maintained by both countries and was “not directed against any third party.” It said its construction and use complied with domestic and international law and would strengthen military cooperation and support regional peace and stability.
Laos’ state news agency KPL reported that officials from both countries described the project at the opening ceremony as the product of cooperation based on mutual respect and equality. The facility would develop Lao military pilots’ practical skills, it said.
The KPL report also said both sides pledged to expand cooperation through joint training and exercises, personnel development and humanitarian assistance. Neither that report nor the Chinese announcement specified how many Chinese military personnel would work at Ban Keun, how long they would remain or the conditions governing Chinese aircraft deployments.
Satellite imagery analysis provided to RFA suggests some construction continued after the opening of the joint airfield. But its future military significance will depend on more than its physical completion, including the extent of Chinese access and the frequency and nature of activities there, Kristanto said.
China already operates military facilities on disputed features in the South China Sea. Ban Keun could extend its overseas presence inland, offering opportunities to build closer ties with the Lao military and gain experience operating from a foreign facility, he said.
The airfield’s immediate military advantages are less clear, analysts said. China has airbases in its own southern territory closer to the South China Sea, raising questions about what additional operations an inland facility in Laos would enable.
In satellite imagery of the airfield during its opening, eight aircraft are visible. Private satellite imagery analyst Jacob Bogle told RFA they were K-8, also known as JL-8, light attack and training aircraft.
Examining an Oct. 7 image, he identified what he thought was one remaining aircraft, while cautioning that the image was blurry. He suggested the others had likely moved into hangars, although their locations could not be established from that observation.
Bogle also identified what appeared to be workshops and temporary construction infrastructure beside the southern end of the runway.
“So while the runway and main buildings are completed, it looks like there is still some minor work that is being finished,” he said.
The imagery does not establish who owns or operates the aircraft. Both China and Laos operate the K-8 type, according to analysts cited by Reuters.
But a Lao military officer, while downplaying concerns over increased Chinese military presence in Southeast Asia, confirmed to RFA that at least some of the fighter jets at the facility are Chinese.
“It is a pilot training airport. A group of people are envious that Laos has a flight training center, yet Laos has never complained about neighboring countries hosting U.S. air bases,” said the officer on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to speak on such matters.
“When Laos built Ban Keun Airport for pilot training, some people overreacted. Naturally, Chinese officials brought their own fighter jets, given that it is a joint Lao-Chinese operation,” he said.
Bogle said it was too early to determine China’s future position at Ban Keun, but that the facility warranted monitoring.
Kristanto said operating combat aircraft from Laos would require substantial investment in fuel storage, maintenance facilities, munitions, air defense and other supporting infrastructure.
“At present, I see little evidence that Ban Keun offers a decisive operational advantage over China’s existing facilities,” he said.
Such limitations do not rule out a broader role in the future. Ban Keun could theoretically support intelligence gathering, surveillance, logistics or forward aircraft deployments if the necessary infrastructure and access arrangements were established, he said.
A sustained Chinese military presence in Laos could add another consideration for neighboring Vietnam, which already faces China across its northern land border and contests Beijing’s claims in the South China Sea.
China’s expansive maritime claims overlap with the exclusive economic zones of Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei and Indonesia. Vietnam also claims the Paracel and Spratly island groups, where competing sovereignty claims are distinct from disputes over rights to surrounding waters. China controls the Paracels, while several governments occupy features in the Spratlys.
In 2016, an international arbitral tribunal rejected China’s claims to the entire South China Sea based on its controversial nine-dash line, which surrounds the whole sea. This claim was seen to exceed what Beijing could legally claim under the U.N. Convention on the Law of the Sea.
Beijing rejected the decision, and has continued to assert its claims over areas that are within the exclusive economic zones of the other claimants.
China has strengthened this position through island-building and military infrastructure, including runways, surveillance equipment and air defenses on occupied reefs. Those facilities support a wider maritime presence in waters where rival claimants seek to protect fishing grounds, energy resources and access to their outposts.
Ban Keun would introduce a different geographic consideration for Hanoi, potentially bringing Chinese military activity to its western side as well.
Bogle argued that facilities in Laos and Cambodia, together with China’s South China Sea bases, had effectively encircled Vietnam.
Kristanto was more cautious. Vietnam would have to account for the possibility of a Chinese military presence beyond its northern border and the South China Sea, he said, but Ban Keun’s inland location and China’s existing airbases limit its immediate operational value.
“For now, I would characterize Ban Keun as a potentially important strategic foothold rather than a major shift in the regional military balance.”
China’s involvement at Cambodia’s Ream naval base shows why a facility’s use over time can be more revealing than its designation as a joint training center, the analysts said.
China financed an expansion of Ream, on Cambodia’s southern coast, where its joint support and training center opened in April 2025. Cambodia maintains that Chinese personnel and warships are not permanently based there.
An analysis published in May 2025 by the Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative documented Chinese naval vessels rotating through Ream after their initial arrival in December 2023.

articles.title_orig: If Elon Musk gifts SpaceX stock through Trump Accounts, it will come with a catch
articles.title_zh: If Elon Musk gifts SpaceX stock through Trump Accounts, it will come with a catch
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk said on Monday that he will give every kid in America a share of SpaceX next year.
He appeared to suggest the gift could land in Trump Accounts — thanking Brad Gerstner, an architect of the program, for "helping enable this" in a comment on X . Posts from the White House and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also referenced Musk's gift as benefiting Trump Accounts.
But if the shares are distributed through the new investment accounts for children, the gift could come with significant strings attached.
Musk's announcement comes weeks after the U.S. Department of the Treasury rolled out guidelines for stock donations to Trump Accounts, also known as 530A accounts. Those include restrictions on selling donated stock: Children who receive it generally cannot sell for five years, even if the company runs into financial trouble.
Treasury's temporary regulations, subject to revision after public comment, aim to encourage stock gifts. But they also give donors unusual influence over children's investments, according to lawyers and philanthropic experts who spoke with CNBC.
In the broader world of charitable giving, donors can typically express preferences about how their gifts are managed, but the receiving organization or trustee retains final authority, said Carolyn Schenck, an attorney and former national fraud counsel at the IRS.
Under the new Trump Account rules, however, it's "the donor that's dictating the terms of the gift," she said.
Representatives for Musk, Gerstner and the Treasury Department did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment on the proposed gift.
According to the Treasury, about 70 million Trump Accounts have been created, including more than 60 million through a recent auto-enrollment effort . Trump Accounts are available to all children with U.S. citizenship under age 18 with valid Social Security numbers.
Musk would be the second philanthropist to publicly announce a stock pledge to Trump Accounts: SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell pledged earlier this summer to use the Trump Account program to gift some 2 million shares . That gift has not yet been distributed.
Trump Account beneficiaries do not have the latitude to sell under circumstances that other investors might otherwise.
Under the new rules, families cannot refuse stock gifted to Trump Accounts and generally cannot sell it until the earlier of five years or the end of the calendar year in which the beneficiary turns 17. Before then, early sales are permitted only in limited circumstances, such as certain corporate transitions or when the stock is formally delisted from a national securities exchange — not when financial or legal problems emerge that might prompt an investor to sell.
"Giving families more choices and more ability to hold the assets that they think are best for them and their kids' future ... would be a good thing," said Adam Michel, director of tax policy studies at the Cato Institute, a libertarian think tank. "But this is not really that, because you have no choice in the asset that is being deposited into your child's account, and then you also have no ability to sell it for the five-year holding period."
The temporary regulations also mandate that if any gifted stock is sold too early, the trustee must purchase the same number and class of shares "as soon as practicable."
This increases beneficiaries' risk of loss if the share price rises before the trustee repurchases the stock, according to Schenck. Beneficiaries would ultimately bear that cost.
"If the fiduciary makes an investment mistake, then the focus is typically restoring value to the beneficiary. But here, the focus seems to be restoring the specific security itself," said Schenck, who left the IRS in 2025 for law firm Caplin & Drysdale.
CNBC has learned the buyback provision is intended to quickly correct trading errors, though the regulations do not explicitly state that purpose or limit the requirement to accidental sales.
The temporary regulations cite donor interests. According to the text, "Donors are attracted by the hope that a stock contribution with a five-year holding period may lead recipients and their families to feel that they have a stake in the fate of the corporation."
Restricting sales virtually eliminates the risk for donors and their companies that Trump Account recipients will sell gifted shares en masse, liquidating a large enough position to depress share prices, according to Jane Ditelberg, chief tax strategist at Northern Trust.
"Certainly, for people who have highly concentrated wealth in a company, and the assets are sitting in their own personal pockets, this makes it a lot easier to give," she said.
Generally speaking, donors can get a bigger tax benefit by gifting appreciated stock to charity than donating cash, as they can claim the charitable deduction and avoid capital gains tax on the gains.
A Treasury official told CNBC that the rules are intended to build long-term wealth for children, especially in lower-income families, and encourage donations. "The major donors we've engaged are motivated by a desire to help children build generational wealth and get a head start on their financial future," the official said in a written statement.
Treasury has said it is in discussions with Trump Accounts donors ranging from "small to mega," but has not identified additional stock pledges since Shotwell's July announcement.
CNBC has identified fewer than a dozen pledges from philanthropists, though about four dozen major employers have committed to seed accounts for their employees' children.
In documents explaining the temporary rules, Treasury pointed to Michael and Susan Dell's $6.25 billion cash pledge and unspecified "similar donations," while acknowledging uncertainty about whether that level of giving will continue. "It is unclear whether this level of giving can be sustained in the long run or whether it is concentrated as Trump accounts are launching," the text states.
Trump Account funds generally may be invested only in low-cost index funds and exchange-traded funds. In the temporary regulations, the Treasury said directly contributed stock is different because it doesn't use account funds for the purchase.
But Ditelberg said a court could conclude that requiring an account to retain individual shares is still an investment decision — an argument that may carry more weight after the Supreme Court's overturning of Chevron deference . Because of the 2024 ruling, courts no longer have to defer to federal agencies' interpretations of statutes when the language is unclear.
"These accounts are going to have to stay invested in those stocks, and the question is whether that's directly contradicting the terms of the statute," she said. "I can't tell you how a court would rule, but I could say there's room for a challenge here."
Ditelberg added that state law grants the right to disclaim an asset. She said it's unclear how the Trump Account donation procedures would accommodate that right.
Schenck noted that Treasury has broad authority to set the terms of Trump Accounts, and it is Treasury — not the original stock donor — that formally requires the shares to be held.
The arrangement also differs from traditional charitable giving. For example, donors who contribute stock to donor-advised funds can recommend how the assets are managed, but the sponsoring charity retains ultimate control, including the authority to sell the shares. This is required to meet the IRS's legal standards for taking a tax deduction on a charitable contribution.
"A key principle is that the charity must have genuine control over the donated assets, including the ability to determine when to sell them, for the gift to qualify as a completed charitable contribution," said Gil Nusbaum, chief administrative and legal officer of National Philanthropic Trust.
Experts say the broader question is whether Treasury's approach aligns with the law Congress enacted.

articles.title_orig: Zelenskiy meets Witkoff as US-Ukraine relations sink to new lows
articles.title_zh: Zelenskiy meets Witkoff as US-Ukraine relations sink to new lows
articles.content_orig:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky says intelligence on early warning systems for Russian strikes "works now" , and that he is "thankful" to the US
The US has previously denied limiting intelligence sharing . Today, the US Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected accusations Ukrainians were dying because the US was withholding intelligence
During a news conference in Oslo after meeting with US special envoy Steve Witkoff, Zelensky also says he is "ready for negotiations" and calls for trilateral talks with the US and Russia - here's what we heard
Speaking from the White House, US President Donald Trump says it is "now time for Ukraine to end this war"
Witkoff will meet with Russian leadership tomorrow and "exchange ideas", Norway's PM Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re says at the conference
The talks come amid deteriorating relations between the Ukrainian leader and US President Donald Trump
Edited by Manish Pandey and Matt Spivey
Paul Adams Diplomatic correspondent
After a torrid ten days, dominated by evidence of another breakdown in relations between Volodymyr Zelensky and Donald Trump, the tone in Oslo seemed curiously upbeat.
The Norwegian prime minister, Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re, said he was glad to have been able to "straighten out a few things" (adding that there was "nothing to gainâ¦from digging into what was said yesterday").
President Zelensky seemed especially pleased with the outcome of a morning conversation with the US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio.
The crucial issues of early warning of Russiaâs ballistic missile strikes had, he suggested, been resolved.
The two men had also discussed Ukraineâs access to Patriot interceptor missiles and Elon Muskâs Starlink system, both vital for Ukraine. Zelensky said he expected "good results".
Finlandâs president, Alexander Stubb, said it had been "a good day for peace", with plenty of progress made "under the radar" on substantive and technical issues.
Steve Witkoff is taking an updated set of proposals to St Petersburg to find out what Vladimir Putin thinks. How long this optimistic moment lasts is anyoneâs guess.
We're now ending our live coverage, but you can keep up to date in our news story.
Bernd Debusmann Jr White House reporter
Trump and Zelensky have had a difficult, up-and-down relationship since the US president came back to the White House, most notably during their tense, fiery meeting in the Oval Office last year.
Their relationship, however, has taken a notable turn over the last few weeks.
It has become increasingly clear that in Trump's eyes, Zelensky is to blame for the ongoing war. A little over a week ago, Trump went as far as to say that Ukraine needs a "new president" to replace him.
We heard more of that today, with Trump saying that the US wants Zelensky to "make a deal" and should have done so already.
He also questioned US support for Ukraine, telling reporters that the US has gotten "absolutely nothing back" for its support "except grief, death and tremendous monetary loss".
Notably, his comments came on the same day Zelensky met with Steve Witkoff and other US representatives in Oslo.
During a news conference, Zelensky said he is "ready for negotiations" and called for trilateral talks with the US and Russia.
Trump's comments will no doubt cause alarm in Kyiv and in European capitals.
It will also sounds alarm in the offices of Washington lawmakers - both Democrats and Republicans - who feel strongly that the US should support Ukraine and who have publicly questioned Trump's policies towards Russia - including his recent waiver on punishing sanctions meant to compel Moscow to come to the table.
Trump was asked by a reporter in the Oval Office about the war in Ukraine
We have just heard from US President Donald Trump, who says the US has given "tremendous" amounts to Ukraine but received nothing back in return.
Speaking from the Oval Office, following an announcement about fraud, the US president says it is time for Ukraine to end the war.
He describes the hatred between Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky as being "tremendous", saying this may be the reason they have been unable to reach a deal.
"We've given a lot to Ukraine. We've gotten absolutely nothing back except grief, death, tremendous monetary loss," Trump says.
As we reported earlier, President Zelensky said in the press conference that he is "thankful" to the US as intelligence on Russian strikes "works now".
Zelensky's adviser Serhii Beskrestnov last week told the BBC that lives had been lost in Ukraine because Kyiv was at the time not receiving reliable US warnings of incoming Russian attacks.
White House officials have said there were no changes to intelligence sharing operations between the two countries.
Earlier today, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected as "scandalous" accusations that Ukrainians were dying because the US was withholding intelligence.
Zelensky told reporters this evening that the early warning systems are important to the Ukrainian people and children as it shows when attacks are incoming.
Serhii Beskrestnov said "people have already died" due to lack of warnings about incoming missile attacks
Zelensky also said restrictions on Ukraine's use of the Starlink internet network were ongoing. He earlier said speed limits had been imposed on Starlink terminals, and that Kyiv had not been told about this in advance.

articles.title_orig: Eight eMudhra CA Keys Compromised, Triggering Emergency Fixes Across Browsers and Software
articles.title_zh: Eight eMudhra CA Keys Compromised, Triggering Emergency Fixes Across Browsers and Software
articles.content_orig:
Security personnel around the world are on high alert Tuesday following the discovery of eight TLS certificates with private keys so weak they could allow anyone to mint trusted browser and app credentials for any site on the Internet.
As of late morning Tuesday, browser makers and some major apps and programming languages had blocked all eight of the intermediate certificates. There are no reports of certificate transparency logs, which track the issuance of all browser-trusted certificates, showing the compromised keys being used maliciously. The threat remains far from over, however, because it will be hard and time-consuming to update other key parts of the Internet, such as Linux distributions and embedded and Internet of Things devices.
The eight intermediate certificates belong to India-based certificate authority eMudhra Limited. An informal advisory published to emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com over on Tuesday posted the message “We have a problem here – Wayne.” The words were digitally signed using the private key of one of the eMudhra certificates. With proof that the reporting party had control of the key, defenders scrambled because the same key could be used to sign unauthorized certificates that would be trusted by millions of servers worldwide.
“This will be a massive cleanup job, bigger than Heartbleed,” Filippo Valsorda, a cryptography engineer and a cryptography maintainer for the open source Go programming language, told Ars. “There will be a very, very long tail, IoT devices, Docker containers, forgotten Linux machines, unmaintained CLI tools that shipped their own copy of the roots (which is common in some ecosystems, like Python). Also, Linux distributions are still rolling out updates, some of them are not ready yet, and then system administrators will need to apply them to a lot of machines.”
Heartbleed is the name of a critical vulnerability in the OpenSSL cryptography library. In 2014, it came under mass exploitation . Exploits let many unaffiliated hackers decrypt TLS-protected exchanges between parties. They also recovered private TLS certificate keys, session cookies, and passwords. The attacks compromised thousands of servers, some belonging to large companies and government agencies around the world.
Recovery required a long series of steps that took years. Steps included patching OpenSSL on all affected devices, reissuing millions of TLS keys, revoking old certificates, rotating passwords and session tokens and updating embedded devices and other forgotten systems—something that was extremely time- and resource-intensive, especially at Internet scale.
“Every time you need a lot of different people in different contexts to do something, it will take a long time,” Valsorda explained. “This time it’s worse because there’s more contexts, more people, and more heterogeneity.”
The compromised eMudhra keys were defective at a level that’s challenging the imagination of many of the engineers studying the incident. A normal size for a NIST P-384 elliptic curve cryptography private key contains roughly 384 bits of entropy, a size allowing almost 2 384 , or a number with 116 digits, different possibilities. The private key sizes of the compromised keys ranged from 3 to 8 bits. Astonishingly, the private keys were 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230, 237.
“That is extremely in the ‘this should not be possible’ category,” Valdorda said. “Maybe some horribly dangerous key generation interface has a ‘size’ parameter and they set it to 1 by mistake???”
Ben Cartwright-Cox, director of BGP.tools, said: “My guess is that it’s example code that accidentally leaked to production, but hard to know. But it’s bonkers that no one noticed.”
At this early stage, the most immediate threat appears to be for those using VPNs, especially in countries with governments likely to maliciously intercept traffic. There are likely many other cases for concern. End users largely have no recourse other than to hold off using many non-browser forms of TLS communication until they receive assurances updates are in place.
As noted, most browsers have already blocked the intermediate certificates. The exception appears to be Edge, which at the time this article went live was still connecting to 12 vulnerable hosts. In response to questions asking why and if the company has plans to do so, a Microsoft representative the company will be in touch if it has anything to “share.” Meanwhile, Signal, WhatsApp, Wireguard, and other apps that don’t rely on TLS for confidentiality aren’t affected. This page and the emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com site show apps known to be patched so far.
The incident is the latest to expose a fatal flaw in the TLS regimen. It’s only as strong as its weakest link, which in this case was eMudhra. Fortunately, transparency logs account for much of that failure, but this measure requires parties to actively monitor massive feeds and works only after unauthorized certificates have been issued. eMudhra representatives weren’t immediately available to answer questions.
One caveat: exploiting compromised certificates requires an active adversary-in-the-middle attack, meaning the attacker must act as a proxy between two TLS parties and receive encrypted traffic, decrypt it, reencrypt it, and send it to the other party. Such capabilities, in some cases, are usually limited to only the most well-resourced attackers. People with control of a local network—at a coffee shop, university, or other organization—face much less of a challenge.

articles.title_orig: Britain says it will carry out defensive air missions over Saudi Arabia
articles.title_zh: Britain says it will carry out defensive air missions over Saudi Arabia
articles.content_orig:
The United Kingdom said Tuesday it will deploy fighter jets to defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by the Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen.
The UK will fly “defensive counter-air missions” using Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets to protect Saudi cities and critical infrastructure, the Defense Ministry said in a statement.
Over the past month, the Houthis have intensified their attacks on Saudi Arabia, launching ballistic missiles and drones at key infrastructure, including oil facilities and airports.
The UK is already providing air-to-air refueling support to Saudi Arabia and has deployed air defense equipment and British personnel to help protect the kingdom, a spokesperson for the prime minister’s office told reporters.
The Typhoons will intercept missiles and drones launched against Saudi Arabia and will not conduct offensive strikes inside Yemen, the spokesperson said.
The conflict has been intensifying since the Houthis announced in July that they would target Saudi shipping in the Red Sea as well as infrastructure inside the kingdom, following a Saudi attack on the Houthi-controlled airport in the Yemeni capital, Sanaa.
They have stepped up their attacks in recent weeks, launching repeated strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport. One such strike killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, making it the deadliest attack on Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.
Saudi Arabia has looked for military support from regional and Western allies to counter the intensified Houthi attacks. France agreed to deploy defense assets, including military personnel, and more than 100 American military advisers are on the ground providing intelligence and targeting support under a newly established joint forces command.
Pakistan has forces stationed in Saudi Arabia, and the Egyptian parliament is debating whether to send support after President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi called an emergency session to deploy military assistance to the kingdom.
“The continuing attacks from the Houthis on our ally Saudi Arabia are absolutely despicable,” UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting said in a statement. “The targeting of the airport in Riyadh in particular shows the lengths the Houthis are going to escalate the situation in the region.”
Last month, the Iran-allied rebel group launched a lightning offensive on Yemen’s western coast, capturing key territory. That included the Bab al-Mandeb maritime chokepoint on the Red Sea, potentially expanding Tehran’s influence over another trade corridor.
Saudi Arabia cancels next week’s ‘Davos in the Desert’ conference after series of Houthi attacks
Backed by Saudi warplanes, Yemen’s anti-Houthi government ground forces have launched a counteroffensive to recapture lost territory. Despite a heavy airstrike campaign and a large ground offensive, Houthi rebels have retained control over key locations and have continued launching missiles and drones at their adversaries.
At least 53 newly recruited Yemeni government forces were killed by the Houthis in a ballistic missile attack Monday on the southeastern Shabwa province, local officials said. More than 200 others were reported wounded.
The attack was condemned by the US mission to Yemen, which called it a “cowardly attack by the Iran-backed Houthi militia” on Yemenis who had “volunteered to keep their communities and country safe.”
This story has been updated with additional developments.
James Frater contributed reporting

articles.title_orig: China built more than twice naval tonnage of US in 2024-25: Euronaval
articles.title_zh: China built more than twice naval tonnage of US in 2024-25: Euronaval
articles.content_orig:
PARIS — China built more than twice the naval tonnage of the United States in the 2024-25 period, narrowing the gap between the two countries’ navies, according to the World Defense Shipbuilding report published by Euronaval ahead of the 2026 edition of the naval defense show.
The combined tonnage of combat ships built by China in the two years through to December 2025 amounted to 636,208 tons, compared to 270,509 tons for the United States, according to data compiled by Flottes de Combat and French maritime industry association Gican.
China accounted for more than a third of the global naval tonnage constructed in 2024-25, based on the Euronaval report. U.S. lawmakers and congressional researchers have warned that China’s greater shipbuilding capacity, combined with delays and bottlenecks in U.S. naval shipbuilding, could hurt America’s ability to keep up with Beijing’s expanding fleet.
“We are seeing a fairly substantial expansion of naval forces, and consequently of shipbuilding,” said Philippe Missoffe, the general director of Gican, in a press briefing here on Tuesday. “We’re seeing an increase in power capabilities, particularly nuclear-powered attack submarines for example.”
Global naval construction overall was booming in the period, with 1.47 million tons of combat vessels built in 2024-25, compared with 959,671 tons in the prior two years. The value of global naval construction amounted to $123.9 billion, climbing from $81.8 billion in 2022-23.
The value of Chinese combat-vessel construction was US$43.5 billion in the latest two-year period, compared with $26.8 billion for the U.S., the report said.
China has reversed roles from 2022-2023, when production of the country’s naval yards amounted to 202,520 tons, compared with 245,703 tons for the U.S., according to the previous edition of the shipbuilding report published in 2024.
The U.S. fleet of combat vessels of more than 200 tons amounted to 3.11 million tons as of Jan. 1, 2026, compared to 1.44 million tons for China’s fleet, the report showed, That compares with 3.22 million tons for the U.S. and 1.3 million tons for China two years earlier.
Russia was in third place in terms of naval construction in 2024-25, with 149,056 tons built, followed by India with 76,430 tons and Italy with 53,700 tons. Turkey, France, Japan, South Korean and Romania rounded out the top 10 of naval builders.
The four-day Euronaval show, the world’s biggest maritime-defense exhibition, is set to kick of in Paris on Nov. 3. The number of exhibitors will be more than 40% higher than in 2024, according to the organizers.
Rudy Ruitenberg is a Europe correspondent for Defense News. He started his career at Bloomberg News and has experience reporting on technology, commodity markets and politics.

articles.content_orig:
Full disclosure: I typically steer away from the build-it-yourself furniture sold on various e-commerce sites.
I’ve been burned one too many times by those seemingly endless kits with a million pieces that somehow refuse to fit together — the hours spent on YouTube tutorials, the headaches, the inevitable realization that I’ve attached one piece wrong and have to start over.
So, building is clearly not for me. But when I came across the LYNSOM 55″ Wide Fluted Dresser on Amazon , I had to stop scrolling. It looked sturdy and modern without being overly trendy — the kind of polished, timeless piece that could fit right into just about any living space without being too “look at me.” And it has four different drawers and four doors for plenty of storage space (a must in NYC).
Then, I read the reviews. If you’ve ever shopped for budget-friendly furniture online, you know that positive reviews are a bit of a rarity. But these ones weren’t just positive, they were glowing. Shoppers are calling it “beautiful and durable” and raving that it’s a “great quality piece.”
Still, it wasn’t the design or glowing reviews that sold me. At under $300, I figured it was worth the gamble— even if it ended up falling apart (for more furniture deals, be sure to check out Way Day , which kicks off on Oct. 24).
Spoiler: it didn’t fall apart.
I did end up having to enlist a friend to help with assembly, and getting the doors just right took some patience, but it was well worth the effort. This piece really is even more beautiful in person, and exceptionally functional for apartment-dwellers.
In my apartment, every inch counts. The last thing I wanted was a bulky dresser that would eat up space. This one strikes a nice balance between style and storage, with four doors and four drawers to stash everything from paperwork and kids’ toys to the everyday clutter I should probably just get rid of.
The curved edges are a nice kid-friendly touch. The round feet give it a slightly more modern vibe. The gold hardware gives it a more expensive, elevated look — my friends suggested it’s “giving West Elm.”
But where this dresser really shines is in a small apartment, especially when you can make a mess disappear in seconds, before guests arrive. For me, that might just be its biggest selling point — along with the price point.
At nearly 50% off, this bestseller holds nearly 2,000 applauding reviews and comes with an ottoman.
